metadata.description: Arm Performix message catalog for en-US locale

JSON_MARSHAL_FAILED.Message: Failed to marshal response to JSON.
JSON_MARSHAL_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot serialize the command output into JSON format.
JSON_MARSHAL_FAILED.Advice: Run the command without the `--json` flag to view the plain text output. If the issue continues when using the `--json` flag, contact Arm support.

INVALID_PID.Message: The PID value you provided is invalid.
INVALID_PID.Explanation: The value `{value}` for the `--pid` flag is invalid. The specified PID must be between `{minPid}` and `{maxPid}`.
INVALID_PID.Advice: Ensure the provided PID value is valid. Run `{cmd} --help` for more information about this flag.

DUPLICATE_SINGULAR_FLAGS.Explanation: This command accepts at most one value for `{flag}`
DUPLICATE_SINGULAR_FLAGS.Advice: Run the command again with only one `{flag}` value

NON_LAUNCH_WORKING_DIR.Message: The `--working-dir` flag can only be used with the `--workload` flag.
NON_LAUNCH_WORKING_DIR.Explanation: The working directory to use can only be specified when launching a new workload to profile.
NON_LAUNCH_WORKING_DIR.Advice: Use the `--workload` flag to specify a workload to launch. The specified working directory will be used for this workload.

NON_LAUNCH_USE_SHELL.Message: The `--use-shell` flag can only be used with the `--workload` flag.
NON_LAUNCH_USE_SHELL.Explanation: The workload can only be run through a shell when launching a new workload to profile.
NON_LAUNCH_USE_SHELL.Advice: Use the `--workload` flag to specify a workload to launch. The workload will be run through a shell.

TARGET_CONVERSION_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot convert the target to a protobuf description.
TARGET_CONVERSION_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot convert information for the target `{target}` to the required format for sending to the server.
TARGET_CONVERSION_FAILED.Advice: Run `target test` to verify that the target machine is properly configured. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

RECIPE_FILES_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot process one or more recipe files:

NO_WORKLOAD_SPECIFIED.Message: You did not specify a workload type.
NO_WORKLOAD_SPECIFIED.Explanation: The `recipe ready` command requires you to specify the type of workload to check using one of these flags: `--pid`, `--workload`, or `--system-wide`. You did not provide any of these flags.
NO_WORKLOAD_SPECIFIED.Advice: Run `recipe ready --help` to learn more about each flag. Provide one workload flag to continue.

NO_WORKLOAD_SPECIFIED.Message: You did not specify a workload type.
NO_WORKLOAD_SPECIFIED.Explanation: The `recipe run` command requires you to specify the type of workload to profile using one of these flags: `--pid`, `--workload`, or `--system-wide`. You did not provide any of these flags.
NO_WORKLOAD_SPECIFIED.Advice: Run `recipe run --help` to learn more about each flag. Provide at least one workload flag to continue.

NON_LAUNCH_ENV_VARS.Message: The `--env` flag can only be used with the `--workload` flag.
NON_LAUNCH_ENV_VARS.Explanation: Environment variables can only be specified when launching a new workload to profile.
NON_LAUNCH_ENV_VARS.Advice: Use the `--workload` flag to specify a workload to launch. The specified environment variables will be exposed to this workload.

VALIDATION_ISSUES.Message: The provided recipe parameters are invalid. Validation issues:

CONFIRM_ALL_PROMPT.Message: Delete all runs? Type 'yes' to confirm.

DELETION_FAILED_NO_SUCCESSES.Message: None of the {numToDelete} runs could be deleted.
DELETION_FAILED_NO_SUCCESSES.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} attempted to delete the {numToDelete} specified runs, but none of them could be deleted.
DELETION_FAILED_NO_SUCCESSES.Advice: Check the message for each failed run for more information. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

DELETION_FAILED_SINGLE_SUCCESS.Message: {numFailures} of the {numToDelete} runs could not be deleted.
DELETION_FAILED_SINGLE_SUCCESS.Explanation: The following runs could not be deleted: {failureIDs}. The other run was deleted successfully.
DELETION_FAILED_SINGLE_SUCCESS.Advice: Check the message for each failed run for more information. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

DELETION_FAILED_PLURAL_SUCCESSES.Message: {numFailures} of the {numToDelete} runs could not be deleted.
DELETION_FAILED_PLURAL_SUCCESSES.Explanation: The following runs could not be deleted: {failureIDs}. The other {numSuccesses} runs were deleted successfully.
DELETION_FAILED_PLURAL_SUCCESSES.Advice: Check the message for each failed run for more information. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

UPDATE_FAILED_MULTIPLE_RUNS.Message: {numFailures} of the {numToUpdate} runs could not be updated.
UPDATE_FAILED_MULTIPLE_RUNS.Explanation: The following runs could not be updated: {failureIDs}.
UPDATE_FAILED_MULTIPLE_RUNS.Advice: Check the message for each failed run for more information. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

NO_OVERRIDE_RECIPE.Message: You must specify a recipe to use with the `override-by-name` recipe selection policy.
NO_OVERRIDE_RECIPE.Explanation: To use the `override-by-name` recipe selection policy, you must specify the name of a recipe to use for rendering.
NO_OVERRIDE_RECIPE.Advice: To specify the recipe name, use the `--recipe` flag. For more information on the available recipe selection policies, run the command with the `--help` flag.

RENDERER_FAILED.Advice: Check the data and settings. Ensure that your system has sufficient resources. Then, try again. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

RENDERER_PENDING.Message: Some renderers did not complete because they have pending dependencies.
RENDERER_PENDING.Explanation: The following renderers did not run, because they depend on data which has not yet been transferred from the target machine: {renderers}
RENDERER_PENDING.Advice: Wait for all pending transfers to complete before retrying the operation.

VISUALIZATION_NOT_FOUND.Message: The visualization with the ID `{id}` does not exist.
VISUALIZATION_NOT_FOUND.Explanation: The recipe used for rendering does not define a visualization with the ID `{id}`.
VISUALIZATION_NOT_FOUND.Advice: Check that any visualizations you specify with the `--visualization` flag are defined by the recipe being used for rendering. To set the recipe to use, use the `--recipe-selection-policy` flag. For more information on these flags, run the command with the `--help` flag.

INDETERMINABLE_MESSAGE.Message: The following compatibility warning was produced when preparing to render:

EMPTY_NAME.Message: The new run name cannot be empty.
EMPTY_NAME.Explanation: You cannot rename a run to an empty string.
EMPTY_NAME.Advice: Enter a non-empty name for the run.

LOG_FILE_OPEN_FAILED.Message: Failed to open the run log file.
LOG_FILE_OPEN_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} failed to open the log file for run `{runId}` at `{filepath}`. The run ID may be invalid or the log file may be missing or unreadable.
LOG_FILE_OPEN_FAILED.Advice: Check that the run ID is valid and verify that the log file exits at the expected location. If the issue persists, contact Arm support.

LOG_FILE_PRINT_ERROR.Message: An error occurred whilst printing the run log.
LOG_FILE_PRINT_ERROR.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} encountered an error when printing the log for run `{runId}` from the file at `{filepath}`.
LOG_FILE_PRINT_ERROR.Advice: Check that the log file is readable and contains valid json. Retry the command with the `--json` arg to print the log file without reformatting. Try a different run to see if the same error occurs. If the issue persists, contact Arm support.

GENERATE_NAME_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot generate a unique target name.
GENERATE_NAME_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} attempted to generate a target name {numAttempts} times, but all generated names were already in use.
GENERATE_NAME_FAILED.Advice: Use the `--name` flag to specify a target name that is not already in use.

COULD_NOT_GET_CONFIG_DIR.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot find the directory used to save the SSH key pair.
COULD_NOT_GET_CONFIG_DIR.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} saves SSH key pairs used for connecting to the target in the directory specified by the `{envVar}` environment variable. This variable is not set, so {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tried to use the system default configuration directory. However, the home directory variable is also not set. {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} needs this variable to expand the relative configuration path to an absolute path.
COULD_NOT_GET_CONFIG_DIR.Advice: Set the home directory variable ('$HOME' on Linux or MacOS, '%USERPROFILE%' on Windows). If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot find the configuration directory, contact Arm support.

COULD_NOT_READ_PUBLIC_KEY.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} generated a new SSH key pair but cannot access the public key.
COULD_NOT_READ_PUBLIC_KEY.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} generated a new SSH key pair and saved the files. However, it cannot access the new public key file at `{path}`.
COULD_NOT_READ_PUBLIC_KEY.Advice: Check that the generated key pair exists at the specified location. Alternatively, create the SSH key pair and provide the private key path, or use `--find-keys` to search for existing keys. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot access the public key, contact Arm support.

NO_TARGET_SPECIFIED.Explanation: The `target remove` command requires that you either specify the name of a target you want to remove, or use the `--all` flag to remove all targets. Neither of these were provided.
NO_TARGET_SPECIFIED.Advice: Provide the name of the target to remove, or use the `--all` flag to remove all targets. Run `target remove --help` for more information.

MISSING_PROPERTY.Message: You must specify at least one property to update.
MISSING_PROPERTY.Explanation: The `target update` command requires that you specify at least one property of the target to update. No flag specifying a property to update was provided.
MISSING_PROPERTY.Advice: Run `target update --help` to see the flags you can use to update the properties of the target. Provide at least one of these flags.

INVALID_FLAG_VALUE.Explanation: The value `{value}` that you entered is not supported for the `{flag}` flag.
INVALID_FLAG_VALUE.Advice: Run the command with the `--help` flag to see the supported values, then use one of those.

FLAG_REQUIRES_FLAG.Explanation: These flags must be provided together, but only `{flag}` was specified.
FLAG_REQUIRES_FLAG.Advice: Provide `{requiredFlag}`, or remove `{flag}`. Run the command with `--help` for more information.

INVALID_AUTH_METHOD.Explanation: The auth value `{value}` that you entered is not a supported authentication method.
INVALID_AUTH_METHOD.Advice: Use `auth=key` or `auth=password`, or omit the auth to default to key authentication. Run the command with `--help` for further information.

PASSWORD_AUTH_WITH_KEY.Message: Password authentication cannot be used with a private key.
PASSWORD_AUTH_WITH_KEY.Explanation: The host `{host}` has been configured with private key path `{key}` and password authentication.
PASSWORD_AUTH_WITH_KEY.Advice: Remove the private key to use password authentication, or switch to key authentication to use the provided key. Run the command with `--help` for further information.

PASSWORD_AUTH_UNSUPPORTED_FLAG.Message: Password authentication does not support the `{flag}` flag.
PASSWORD_AUTH_UNSUPPORTED_FLAG.Explanation: The target configuration uses password authentication, which is incompatible with the `{flag}` flag.
PASSWORD_AUTH_UNSUPPORTED_FLAG.Advice: Remove `{flag}` to use password authentication, or switch to key authentication. Run the command with `--help` for further information.

MUTUALLY_EXCLUSIVE_FLAGS.Explanation: You cannot combine these flags. Use only one per command.
MUTUALLY_EXCLUSIVE_FLAGS.Advice: Choose one flag. Run `{cmd} --help` to learn more about each flag.

INVALID_PORT_RANGE.Message: The port value you provided is invalid.
INVALID_PORT_RANGE.Explanation: The value `{provided}` for the `{name}` flag is invalid. The port number must be a valid TCP port between `{min}` and `{max}`.
INVALID_PORT_RANGE.Advice: Ensure the provided port number is valid and try again.

INVALID_ENV_VAR.Message: The environment variable definition `{envVarString}` is invalid.
INVALID_ENV_VAR.Explanation: `{envVarString}` cannot be parsed as a name-value pair.
INVALID_ENV_VAR.Advice: Ensure environment variables are specified in the format `KEY=value`.

GET_VERSION_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} connected to the daemon but the version query failed due to an internal error.
GET_VERSION_FAILED.Advice: Retry the command. If the problem continues, restart the daemon. If the issue persists, contact Arm support.

SERVER_AUTH_PORTS_MUST_DIFFER.Message: The server and auth ports must be different.
SERVER_AUTH_PORTS_MUST_DIFFER.Explanation: Both `--server-port` and `--auth-port` were set to the same value. Each service must run on a different port.
SERVER_AUTH_PORTS_MUST_DIFFER.Advice: Choose distinct port numbers for the main service and the auth service.

READINESS_READY.Message: The recipe is ready to be run on your target machine. Informational messages:

READINESS_WARNING.Message: The recipe is ready to be run on your target machine, with the following warnings:

READINESS_ERROR.Message: The recipe is not ready to be run on your target machine, due to the following problems:

READINESS_UNKNOWN.Message: The recipe might not be ready to be run on your target machine. One or more of the following readiness messages have unknown severity:

CREATE_KNOWN_HOSTS_FILE.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot create the SSH known hosts file.
CREATE_KNOWN_HOSTS_FILE.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} encountered an error creating the SSH known hosts file at `{path}` on the host. The system creates the file if it does not exist, but the parent directory must already exist and be writable.
CREATE_KNOWN_HOSTS_FILE.Advice: Check that you have write permissions for the specified path. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot create the known hosts file, contact Arm support.

CREATE_SSH_DIR.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot create the SSH key storage directory.
CREATE_SSH_DIR.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot create the SSH key storage directory at `{path}`. One possible cause is that the path is not writable.
CREATE_SSH_DIR.Advice: Check that the parent directory at `{path}` is writable. Alternatively, you can create the SSH key pair manually, and specify the private key path. To search for existing keys, use the `--find-keys` flag. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot create the directory, contact Arm support.

KEY_ALREADY_EXISTS.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot create a new SSH `{keyType}` key.
KEY_ALREADY_EXISTS.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} generated a random filename `{name}` for the SSH `{keyType}` key, but a file with that name already exists in `{dir}`.
KEY_ALREADY_EXISTS.Advice: Because the filename is randomly generated, trying the operation again might succeed. Alternatively, create the SSH key pair manually and specify the private key path. To search for existing keys, use the `--find-keys` flag. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot create the key, contact Arm support.

GENERATE_RSA_KEY_PAIR.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot generate the SSH RSA key pair.
GENERATE_RSA_KEY_PAIR.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot generate the RSA key pair due to an internal error.
GENERATE_RSA_KEY_PAIR.Advice: This error might indicate a deeper issue. Repeat the operation to see if the error occurs again. If it does, contact Arm support so that we can investigate the cause. As a temporary workaround, you can create the SSH key pair manually and specify the private key path. You can also use the `--find-keys` flag to locate existing keys.

WRITE_KEY_FILE.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot create the SSH `{keyType}` key file.
WRITE_KEY_FILE.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot write the generated `{keyType}` key to `{path}`.
WRITE_KEY_FILE.Advice: Check that you have write permissions for `{path}`. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot create the key file, contact Arm support.

CONNECT_WITH_PASSWORD.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot establish an SSH connection to the target using password authentication.
CONNECT_WITH_PASSWORD.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect to the target using the password provided. Possible causes include the SSH server being unreachable, unresponsive, or rejecting the SSH credentials.
CONNECT_WITH_PASSWORD.Advice: Check that the SSH server is listening on the expected port and that the provided credentials are valid. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot connect to the target, contact Arm support.

CANNOT_APPEND_TO_AUTHORIZED_KEYS.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot add the generated SSH public key to `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` on the target.
CANNOT_APPEND_TO_AUTHORIZED_KEYS.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} generated an SSH key pair, and connected to the target using the provided credentials. However, it cannot add the public key to `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`.
CANNOT_APPEND_TO_AUTHORIZED_KEYS.Advice: If `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` already exists, ensure that it and its parent directories are writable. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot add the public key, contact Arm support.

CLIENT_CERT_UNAVAILABLE.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot load the CLI client TLS certificate.
CLIENT_CERT_UNAVAILABLE.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} looked for the CLI client certificate that matches the current TLS certificate authority, but it could not be found or verified.
CLIENT_CERT_UNAVAILABLE.Advice: Ensure the {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} configuration directory is readable, restart the daemon to create a new certificate authority, then retry the operation. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

CLIENT_CERT_WRITE_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot store the CLI client TLS certificate.
CLIENT_CERT_WRITE_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} failed to write the CLI client certificate to disk with `{perms}` permissions. Possible causes include insufficient permissions or a full disk.
CLIENT_CERT_WRITE_FAILED.Advice: Ensure the {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} configuration directory is writable, then retry the operation. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

CLIENT_KEY_WRITE_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot store the CLI client TLS private key.
CLIENT_KEY_WRITE_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} failed to write the CLI client private key to disk with `{perms}` permissions. Possible causes include insufficient permissions or a full disk.
CLIENT_KEY_WRITE_FAILED.Advice: Ensure the {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} configuration directory is writable, then retry the operation. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

CLIENT_CERT_ENCODE_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot store the CLI client TLS certificate.
CLIENT_CERT_ENCODE_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tried to encode the CLI client certificate while trying to write it to disk, but it failed because the certificate data is missing.
CLIENT_CERT_ENCODE_FAILED.Advice: Restart the daemon to create a new certificate authority, then retry the operation. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

CLIENT_KEY_ENCODE_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot encode the CLI client TLS private key.
CLIENT_KEY_ENCODE_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} only supports ECDSA for TLS private keys, but the key type `{keyType}` was provided.
CLIENT_KEY_ENCODE_FAILED.Advice: Restart the daemon to create a new certificate authority, then retry the operation. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect to the authentication service.
SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tried to connect to the authentication service on the daemon, but failed to establish a connection within the {timeout} second timeout. This might be because the service is not running, the daemon is not running, the daemon is running as a different user to the one that ran the command, or the network is not reachable.
SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE.Advice: Check that the daemon is running and was launched by user {user}, then retry the operation. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

STREAM_FAILURE.Message: The {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} CLI client lost the connection to the engine while logging in to the target.
STREAM_FAILURE.Explanation: The connection to the engine closed unexpectedly, possibly because the background service stopped or the connection was interrupted.
STREAM_FAILURE.Advice: Restart the daemon, then retry the operation. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

PROMPT_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not read the user credentials.
PROMPT_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} performed an action that required authentication with the target. The credential prompt did not complete successfully during login to the target.
PROMPT_FAILED.Advice: Retry the operation and check that the credential prompt appears. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

HOST_KEY_MAX_ATTEMPTS.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} did not receive a valid host key confirmation after multiple attempts.
HOST_KEY_MAX_ATTEMPTS.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} asked for confirmation of the target host key, but the maximum number of attempts was reached without a valid response.
HOST_KEY_MAX_ATTEMPTS.Advice: Retry the operation and respond with `yes`, `no`, or the expected fingerprint. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

CANNOT_START_NEW_SERVER.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot start a new server. This might be because a server is already running.
CANNOT_START_NEW_SERVER.Advice: Run `daemon stop` to stop any existing server, then retry the operation. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot start a new server, contact Arm support.

LIST_ANDROID_PACKAGE_ACTIVITIES.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot collect Android package activities from the target.
LIST_ANDROID_PACKAGE_ACTIVITIES.Explanation: The target agent could not inspect Android package resolver data to find activities registered for the `android.intent.action.MAIN` intent.
LIST_ANDROID_PACKAGE_ACTIVITIES.Advice: Check that the Android target is connected and that `dumpsys package r` is available on the target. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

LIST_ANDROID_PACKAGES.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot collect Android packages from the target.
LIST_ANDROID_PACKAGES.Explanation: The target agent could not list third-party Android packages installed on the target.
LIST_ANDROID_PACKAGES.Advice: Check that the Android target is connected and that `pm list packages -3` works on the target. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

LIST_PROCESSES.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot collect the list of running processes on the target.
LIST_PROCESSES.Explanation: This operation needs access to the list of processes running on the target. {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot read the `/proc` directory to get this information. Possible causes include permission issues or a problem with the file system.
LIST_PROCESSES.Advice: Make sure that the `/proc` directory exists on the target system and that you have permission to read from it. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM.Message: This operation is not supported on {platform} targets.
UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM.Explanation: The target agent does not currently support this system information operation on this target platform.
UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM.Advice: Use a target platform that supports this operation.

STARTUP_FAILED.Explanation: An internal error occurred while starting the agent as 'controller'.
STARTUP_FAILED.Advice: Retry the operation. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM.Message: The 'root worker' agent role is not supported on this platform.
UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM.Explanation: The {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} agent cannot run as a 'root worker' on {os} {arch}.
UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM.Advice: Use a supported OS and architecture combination. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM.Message: The 'group controller' agent role is not supported on this platform.
UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM.Explanation: The {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} agent cannot run as a 'group controller' on {os} {arch}.
UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM.Advice: Use a supported OS and architecture combination. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

INVALID_PATH.Message: The agent deploy root path is empty.
INVALID_PATH.Explanation: The agent deploy root path must be set to resolve where files will be written on the host.
INVALID_PATH.Advice: Retry the operation. If the issue persists, contact Arm support.

MISSING_USER.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot resolve the agent deploy root because a user name is unavailable.
MISSING_USER.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot use the HOME directory as the deploy root and cannot determine the user name required for the fallback directory.
MISSING_USER.Advice: Retry the operation. If the issue persists, contact Arm support.

WIN_MISSING_TEMP.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot resolve the agent deploy root because a temporary directory is unavailable.
WIN_MISSING_TEMP.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not use LOCALAPPDATA for the deploy root and no temporary directory was available to use instead.
WIN_MISSING_TEMP.Advice: Retry the operation. If the issue persists, contact Arm support.

PROOF_MECHANISM_UNKNOWN.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not elevate privileges on the target.
PROOF_MECHANISM_UNKNOWN.Explanation: The {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} agent does not recognize the specified privilege proof mechanism.
PROOF_MECHANISM_UNKNOWN.Advice: Use a supported privilege proof mechanism. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

PROOF_MECHANISM_NOT_SUPPORTED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not elevate privileges on the target.
PROOF_MECHANISM_NOT_SUPPORTED.Explanation: The privilege proof mechanism {mech} is not supported on this target.
PROOF_MECHANISM_NOT_SUPPORTED.Advice: Use a supported privilege proof mechanism. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

GENERATE_TOKEN_FAILED.Message: Could not elevate privileges on the target.
GENERATE_TOKEN_FAILED.Explanation: The {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} agent could not generate a privilege elevation token.
GENERATE_TOKEN_FAILED.Advice: If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

ROOT_WORKER_START_FAILED.Message: Could not elevate privileges on the target.
ROOT_WORKER_START_FAILED.Explanation: The {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} agent could not start a root worker process to handle privileged operations.
ROOT_WORKER_START_FAILED.Advice: If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

NO_ROOT_WORKER_FOUND.Message: Could not execute the recipe command on target with elevated privileges.
NO_ROOT_WORKER_FOUND.Explanation: The {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} agent could not find a root worker process to handle privileged operations.
NO_ROOT_WORKER_FOUND.Advice: If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

INVALID_TOKEN.Message: Could not execute the recipe command on target with elevated privileges.
INVALID_TOKEN.Explanation: The {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} agent received an invalid privilege proof token.
INVALID_TOKEN.Advice: If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

MECHANISM_PASSWORDLESS_SUDO.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not elevate privileges using passwordless sudo.
MECHANISM_PASSWORDLESS_SUDO.Explanation: Privilege elevation using passwordless sudo failed on the target.
MECHANISM_PASSWORDLESS_SUDO.Advice: Check that passwordless sudo is correctly configured on the target. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

INTERNAL_ERROR.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not process the API request.
INTERNAL_ERROR.Explanation: The agent encountered an unexpected internal error while processing the {request} API request.
INTERNAL_ERROR.Advice: Retry the operation. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

MISSING_LAUNCH_REQUEST.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not process the API request.
MISSING_LAUNCH_REQUEST.Explanation: The request to launch a new process is missing required parameters.
MISSING_LAUNCH_REQUEST.Advice: Check that the request includes all required parameters. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

MISSING_COMMAND.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not handle the API request.
MISSING_COMMAND.Explanation: The {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} agent received an API request to launch a new process, but the request did not include the required command string.
MISSING_COMMAND.Advice: If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

CREATE_TEMP_DIR_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not create a temporary directory at `{path}` on the target.
CREATE_TEMP_DIR_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tried to create a temporary directory at `{path}` with standard permissions on the target, but the operation failed. Possible causes include insufficient permissions or a full or read-only file system.
CREATE_TEMP_DIR_FAILED.Advice: Verify that the target file system is writable and has enough free space. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

MKDIR_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not create the directory `{path}` on the target.
MKDIR_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} attempted to create the directory `{path}` with standard permissions, but the operation failed. Possible causes include insufficient permissions, an existing file with the same name, or file system restrictions.
MKDIR_FAILED.Advice: Check the target path and permissions, then try again. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

RM_STAT_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not remove `{path}` because it cannot read its metadata.
RM_STAT_FAILED.Explanation: Before removing `{path}`, {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tried to read its metadata but encountered an error. Possible causes include the path not existing or lacking permissions.
RM_STAT_FAILED.Advice: Verify that `{path}` exists and that you have permission to access it. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

RM_DIR_NON_RECURSIVE.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot remove the directory `{path}` without recursive deletion.
RM_DIR_NON_RECURSIVE.Explanation: The remove operation was requested without the recursive option, but `{path}` is a directory. The recursive option is required to remove directories.
RM_DIR_NON_RECURSIVE.Advice: Enable recursive deletion if you want to remove the directory and its contents.

RM_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not remove `{path}` on the target.
RM_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tried to remove `{path}`, but the file system returned an error. Possible causes include permissions issues or the path being in use.
RM_FAILED.Advice: Check that the path exists, is not in use, and that you have permission to remove it. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

MAKE_WRITABLE_STAT_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not change permissions for `{path}` because it cannot read its metadata.
MAKE_WRITABLE_STAT_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tried to read file information for `{path}` before making it writable, but the operation failed. Possible causes include the path not existing or insufficient permissions.
MAKE_WRITABLE_STAT_FAILED.Advice: Verify that `{path}` exists and is accessible, then try again. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

MAKE_WRITABLE_ENCODE_PATH_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not make `{path}` writable on Windows.
MAKE_WRITABLE_ENCODE_PATH_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tried to convert `{path}` to the required Windows path format before clearing the read-only attribute, but the conversion failed. Possible causes include invalid characters in the path.
MAKE_WRITABLE_ENCODE_PATH_FAILED.Advice: Provide a valid Windows path and try again. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

MAKE_WRITABLE_GET_ATTR_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not read the file attributes for `{path}` on Windows.
MAKE_WRITABLE_GET_ATTR_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} attempted to read the Windows file attributes for `{path}` before changing permissions, but the call failed. Possible causes include the file not existing or insufficient permissions.
MAKE_WRITABLE_GET_ATTR_FAILED.Advice: Verify that `{path}` exists and is accessible on the target. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

MAKE_WRITABLE_WALK_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not traverse `{path}` while making files writable.
MAKE_WRITABLE_WALK_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} attempted to recursively clear the read-only attribute under `{path}`, but encountered an error while traversing the directory tree.
MAKE_WRITABLE_WALK_FAILED.Advice: Check permissions on `{path}` and its children, then try again.

MAKE_WRITABLE_SET_ATTR_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not update file attributes for `{path}` on Windows.
MAKE_WRITABLE_SET_ATTR_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tried to clear the read-only attribute on `{path}`, but updating the attributes failed.
MAKE_WRITABLE_SET_ATTR_FAILED.Advice: Ensure the path exists and is accessible. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

LIST_FILES_UNEXPECTED_FILEINFO.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not read file information for `{path}`.
LIST_FILES_UNEXPECTED_FILEINFO.Explanation: The system returned an unexpected file information structure for `{path}` while listing files.
LIST_FILES_UNEXPECTED_FILEINFO.Advice: Try the operation again. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

COMMON_PERMISSION_ERROR.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not handle the file system operation `{operation}` due to a permissions error.
COMMON_PERMISSION_ERROR.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tried to perform `{operation}` on `{path}`, but the operation failed due to insufficient permissions or access rights.
COMMON_PERMISSION_ERROR.Advice: Ensure the operation has sufficient permissions and access rights on the target, then try again. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

TRANSPORT_ERROR.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} lost communication with the agent on the target.
TRANSPORT_ERROR.Explanation: The communication channel between {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} and the agent failed. This may be due to network issues, the target shutting down, or the agent process exiting.
TRANSPORT_ERROR.Advice: Check that the target is running and its network connection is stable, then run the recipe again. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

ACK_TIMEOUT.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} can no longer confirm that the agent on the target is responsive.
ACK_TIMEOUT.Explanation: The agent did not acknowledge its presence in the allotted time. This may be due to network issues, the target being overloaded, or the agent process crashing.
ACK_TIMEOUT.Advice: Check the target's network connection is stable and compute resources are sufficient before running the recipe again. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

SHUTTING_DOWN.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect to the agent server on the target.
SHUTTING_DOWN.Explanation: The {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} server cannot connect to the agent on the target, because the local server is shutting down.
SHUTTING_DOWN.Advice: Repeat the operation to start up a new {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} server. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot connect to the agent server, contact Arm support.

INSUFFICIENT_PRIVILEGES.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not start the agent server on the {locality}.
INSUFFICIENT_PRIVILEGES.Explanation: The agent server must run with administrator or root privileges, but privilege elevation is not allowed on the {locality}.
INSUFFICIENT_PRIVILEGES.Advice: Check that privilege elevation, such as `sudo`, is configured correctly on the {locality}. For more information, see 'Prepare your target for {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} connections' in the {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} User Guide. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot start the agent server, contact Arm support.

AGENT_NOT_DEPLOYED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not find the launch script for the agent server on the target.
AGENT_NOT_DEPLOYED.Explanation: This operation requires a running agent server. {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tried to run `{cmd}` in `{workingDir}`, but the script was missing. The {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tools might be missing from the target or they might have been manually modified.
AGENT_NOT_DEPLOYED.Advice: Run `target prepare` to deploy the agent. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot launch the agent server, contact Arm support.

HOST_AGENT_NOT_DEPLOYED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not locate the launch script for the agent server on the host.
HOST_AGENT_NOT_DEPLOYED.Explanation: This operation requires a running agent server. {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tried to run `{cmd}` in `{workingDir}`, but the script was missing. The {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tools might be missing from the host or they might have been manually modified.
HOST_AGENT_NOT_DEPLOYED.Advice: Run a recipe that deploys host-side tools with `--deploy-tools` to deploy the host agent. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot launch the agent server, contact Arm support.

LAUNCH_ERROR_CODE.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not launch the agent server on the {locality}.
LAUNCH_ERROR_CODE.Explanation: This operation requires a running agent server. {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tried to run `{cmd}` in `{workingDir}`, but it returned exit code `{exitCode}`. Possible causes include resource limits such insufficient memory or file descriptors, an internal script error, or manual changes to the {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tools directory.
LAUNCH_ERROR_CODE.Advice: Check the {locality} has sufficient resources to run the agent server. Ensure the {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tools directory has not been manually modified. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot launch the agent server, contact Arm support.

RUN_LAUNCH_COMMAND.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not launch the agent server on the {locality}.
RUN_LAUNCH_COMMAND.Explanation: This operation requires a running agent server. {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tried to run `{cmd}` in `{workingDir}`, but an error occurred. Possible causes include the script not being executable, resource limits such as insufficient memory or file descriptors, a broken connection to the {locality}, or manual changes to the {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tools directory.
RUN_LAUNCH_COMMAND.Advice: Ensure that the '{cmd}' script exists and is executable. Check that the {locality} has sufficient resources to run the agent server. Ensure that the {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tools directory has not been manually modified. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot launch the agent server, contact Arm support.

NEW_AGENT_CONNECTION.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not connect to the agent server on the {locality}.
NEW_AGENT_CONNECTION.Explanation: This operation needs a running {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} agent server on the {locality}. {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} launched a new agent but could not connect to it. The agent might have shut down or there might be a connection issue.
NEW_AGENT_CONNECTION.Advice: Try the operation again. Check that the agent server is listening on port `{portNum}`. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot connect to the agent server, contact Arm support.

MISSING_TEMP_DIR.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot locate the TEMP directory on the Windows target.
MISSING_TEMP_DIR.Explanation: This operation needs the TEMP directory to store temporary files on the Windows target. {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not find the TEMP directory because the TEMP environment variable is not defined or is inaccessible.
MISSING_TEMP_DIR.Advice: Ensure that the TEMP environment variable is defined on the target and points to a valid directory. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot locate the TEMP directory, contact Arm support.

AGENT_TARGET_INFO_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot collect information from the target.
AGENT_TARGET_INFO_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not run the `{cmdName}` tool because it is not deployed on the target.
AGENT_TARGET_INFO_FAILED.Advice: Use `target prepare` to deploy the tool. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot collect information from the target, contact Arm support.

PROBE_TOOL_NOT_DEPLOYED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot collect information from the target.
PROBE_TOOL_NOT_DEPLOYED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not run the `{cmdName}` tool because it is not deployed on the target.
PROBE_TOOL_NOT_DEPLOYED.Advice: Use `target prepare` to deploy the tool. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot collect information from the target, contact Arm support.

RUN_PROBE.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot collect information from the target.
RUN_PROBE.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} ran the `{cmdName}` command (`{fullCmd}`) on the target to collect the required target information, but the command failed. This might be due to a loss of connection to the target agent.
RUN_PROBE.Advice: Try the operation again. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot collect information from the target, contact Arm support.

TARGET_IN_USE.Message: The target is currently in use.
TARGET_IN_USE.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} needs to run the `{cmdName}` tool on the target to collect target information, but this tool is already running on the target. Another user might be profiling this machine currently.
TARGET_IN_USE.Advice: Wait for the target to become available, then try again. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot collect information from the target, contact Arm support.

PROBE_ERROR_CODE.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot collect information from the target.
PROBE_ERROR_CODE.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} ran the `{cmdName}` command (`{fullCmd}`) on the target to collect the required target information, but the command returned the exit code `{exitCode}`. The tool might not be executable, or the system might have run out of resources.
PROBE_ERROR_CODE.Advice: Check that the tool exists at `{toolPath}` and that you can run it. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot collect information from the target, contact Arm support.

RETRIEVE_PROBE_FILE.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot collect information from the target.
RETRIEVE_PROBE_FILE.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} ran the `{cmdName}` tool, which saved data to `{responsePath}` on the target. An error occurred while trying to read this file and send it to the host. The file might be missing, unreadable, or the target connection might have failed.
RETRIEVE_PROBE_FILE.Advice: Check whether the file at `{responsePath}` exists and is readable. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

PROBE_FILE_UNMARSHAL.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot collect information from the target.
PROBE_FILE_UNMARSHAL.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} ran the `{cmdName}` tool on the target, which saved output as a JSON file at `{responsePath}`. {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not parse this file due to formatting issues or data corruption.
PROBE_FILE_UNMARSHAL.Advice: If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot collect information from the target, contact Arm support.

RUN_LSCPU.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot collect CPU information from the target.
RUN_LSCPU.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} ran the `lscpu` command on the target to collect the required CPU information, but the command failed. This might be due to a loss of connection to the target agent.
RUN_LSCPU.Advice: Try the operation again. Check if you can manually run `lscpu` on the target. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot collect information from the target, contact Arm support.

LSCPU_ERROR_CODE.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot collect CPU information from the target.
LSCPU_ERROR_CODE.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} ran the `lscpu` command on the target to collect the required CPU information, but the command returned the exit code `{exitCode}`.
LSCPU_ERROR_CODE.Advice: Check if you can manually run `lscpu` on the target. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot run this command, contact Arm support.

IDENTIFY_CPUS_FROM_OUTPUT.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot identify the CPU on the target.
IDENTIFY_CPUS_FROM_OUTPUT.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} used the `lscpu` command to identify CPU information about the target, but it cannot extract this information from the command output.
IDENTIFY_CPUS_FROM_OUTPUT.Advice: Check that the output of running `lscpu` on the target includes the number of CPUs, and the CPU model name. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot identify this information, contact Arm support.

RUN_COMMAND.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot collect information from the Windows target.
RUN_COMMAND.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tried to run the PowerShell command `{command}` on the target, but the command failed to start.
RUN_COMMAND.Advice: Check that PowerShell is installed on the target, then try again. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

COMMAND_ERROR_CODE.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot collect information from the Windows target.
COMMAND_ERROR_CODE.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} ran the PowerShell command `{command}` on the target, but it returned the exit code `{exitCode}`.
COMMAND_ERROR_CODE.Advice: Check that PowerShell is installed on the target, then try again. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

PARSE_OS_INFO.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot parse the Windows OS information returned by PowerShell.
PARSE_OS_INFO.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} ran the PowerShell command `{command}` on the target, but the output was not in the expected format.
PARSE_OS_INFO.Advice: Run `{command}` directly on the target and confirm that it prints `ProductName|Version|Build`. If the command output is empty or does not match the expected format, save the output and contact Arm support with the details.

PARSE_CPU_INFO.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot parse the Windows CPU information returned by PowerShell.
PARSE_CPU_INFO.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} ran the PowerShell command `{command}` on the target, but the output was not in the expected format.
PARSE_CPU_INFO.Advice: Run `{command}` directly on the target and confirm that it prints `ProcessorName|LogicalProcessors|PhysicalProcessors`. If the command output is empty or does not match the expected format, save the output and contact Arm support with the details.

PARSE_ARCH_INFO.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot determine the processor architecture of the Windows target.
PARSE_ARCH_INFO.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} ran the PowerShell command `{command}` on the target, but the output was not in the expected format.
PARSE_ARCH_INFO.Advice: Run `{command}` directly on the target and confirm that it prints the processor architecture (for example, `ARM64`). If the command returns an empty or different value, save the output and contact Arm support with the details.

CREATE_ROOT_CA_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot create the TLS root certificate authority.
CREATE_ROOT_CA_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tried to create a new TLS root certificate authority for mutual authentication but the operation failed.
CREATE_ROOT_CA_FAILED.Advice: Restart the daemon to create a new certificate authority, then retry the operation. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

CREATE_SERVER_CERT_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot create the TLS server certificate.
CREATE_SERVER_CERT_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tried to create a TLS server certificate signed by the root certificate authority but the operation failed.
CREATE_SERVER_CERT_FAILED.Advice: Restart the daemon to create a new server certificate, then retry the operation. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

LOAD_ROOT_CA_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot load the TLS root certificate authority.
LOAD_ROOT_CA_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not read the TLS root certificate or private key from disk. The files might be missing or corrupted.
LOAD_ROOT_CA_FAILED.Advice: Restart the daemon to create a new certificate authority, then retry the operation. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

CREATE_CLIENT_CERT_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot create the TLS client certificate.
CREATE_CLIENT_CERT_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tried to create a TLS client certificate signed by the root certificate authority but the operation failed.
CREATE_CLIENT_CERT_FAILED.Advice: Restart the client to create a new client certificate, then retry the operation. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

LOAD_SERVER_CREDENTIALS_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot load the TLS server certificate credentials.
LOAD_SERVER_CREDENTIALS_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not load the TLS server certificate or private key from disk.
LOAD_SERVER_CREDENTIALS_FAILED.Advice: Restart the daemon to create a new server certificate, then retry the operation. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

ROOT_CA_UNAVAILABLE.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot find the TLS root certificate authority.
ROOT_CA_UNAVAILABLE.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} waited for the TLS certificate authority files to appear but they were not found before the timeout elapsed.
ROOT_CA_UNAVAILABLE.Advice: Restart the daemon to create a new certificate authority, then retry the operation. If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

RUN_ID_EMPTY.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot open the Streamline report because it does not include a run identifier.
RUN_ID_EMPTY.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} requires a Streamline run identifier in the run data, but none was found.
RUN_ID_EMPTY.Advice: Check that the run was captured or exported correctly. If the run data is incomplete, repeat the capture and export the run again.

MODEL_NIL.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot open the Streamline report because it does not include a run model.
MODEL_NIL.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} uses the run model to locate the Streamline capture files, but none was supplied.
MODEL_NIL.Advice: Ensure that the renderer supplies the run model when opening the report.

SL_OPEN_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not initialize the Streamline runtime.
SL_OPEN_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not initialize the Streamline runtime. The call returned `{slReturnCode}`.
SL_OPEN_FAILED.Advice: Verify that the Streamline libraries are installed and compatible with your platform. If they are, run the initialization again.

CANCELLATION_PREDICATE_CREATE_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not create the Streamline cancellation predicate.
CANCELLATION_PREDICATE_CREATE_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not create the Streamline cancellation predicate. The call returned `{slReturnCode}`.
CANCELLATION_PREDICATE_CREATE_FAILED.Advice: Verify the Streamline installation and try the operation again.

PROGRESS_MONITOR_CREATE_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not create the Streamline progress monitor.
PROGRESS_MONITOR_CREATE_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not create the Streamline progress monitor. The call returned `{slReturnCode}`.
PROGRESS_MONITOR_CREATE_FAILED.Advice: Verify the Streamline installation, then try the operation again.

AVAILABLE_REPORT_GROUPS_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not read the Streamline report groups.
AVAILABLE_REPORT_GROUPS_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not enumerate the report groups from the Streamline capture. The call returned `{slReturnCode}`.
AVAILABLE_REPORT_GROUPS_FAILED.Advice: Check the capture files and verify that the Streamline libraries are functioning correctly.

SYMBOL_TABLE_OPEN_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not open the Streamline symbol table.
SYMBOL_TABLE_OPEN_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not open a Streamline symbol table. The call returned `{slReturnCode}`.
SYMBOL_TABLE_OPEN_FAILED.Advice: Ensure that the capture files are not corrupted, then try the operation again.

SYMBOL_ITERATOR_CREATE_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not create the Streamline symbol iterator.
SYMBOL_ITERATOR_CREATE_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not create a Streamline symbol iterator. The call returned `{slReturnCode}`.
SYMBOL_ITERATOR_CREATE_FAILED.Advice: Ensure that the capture files are not corrupted, then try the operation again.

SYMBOL_ITERATOR_GET_ITEM_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not read a symbol from the Streamline capture.
SYMBOL_ITERATOR_GET_ITEM_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not read the next symbol from the Streamline iterator. The call returned `{slReturnCode}`.
SYMBOL_ITERATOR_GET_ITEM_FAILED.Advice: Ensure that the capture files are not corrupted, then try the operation again.

REPORT_OPEN_FAILED.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not open the Streamline report.
REPORT_OPEN_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not open the Streamline report. The call returned `{slReturnCode}`.
REPORT_OPEN_FAILED.Advice: Ensure that the capture files exist at `{path}` and that the Streamline libraries are installed correctly.

REPORT_ENTRY_NIL.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not use the Streamline report because the report entry is missing.
REPORT_ENTRY_NIL.Explanation: A Streamline report entry was missing when {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} requested a report handle.
REPORT_ENTRY_NIL.Advice: Contact Arm support with details of the renderer that produced the error.

CAPTURE_COMPONENT_NOT_FOUND.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} could not locate the Streamline capture for run `{runId}`.
CAPTURE_COMPONENT_NOT_FOUND.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} expected the Streamline capture to appear in the run manifest, but it is missing for run `{runId}`.
CAPTURE_COMPONENT_NOT_FOUND.Advice: Verify that the run contains a `capture.apc` component. If the issue continues, regenerate the run or contact Arm support.

INVALID_PORT_FORMAT.Message: The specified port format is invalid.
INVALID_PORT_FORMAT.Explanation: The port number `{portNum}` provided for `{jumpNode}` is not a positive integer.
INVALID_PORT_FORMAT.Advice: Ensure that the port number is a positive integer.

CREATE_SFTP_CLIENT.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot create an SFTP client connection to the target.
CREATE_SFTP_CLIENT.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} connected to the target using SSH, but could not start an SFTP connection. The SFTP connection is required to transfer information from the target to the host.
CREATE_SFTP_CLIENT.Advice: If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot create an SFTP client connection to the target, contact Arm support.

UNSUPPORTED_TARGET_OS.Message: The target platform is not supported.
UNSUPPORTED_TARGET_OS.Explanation: The target machine is running an unsupported operating system ({os}).
UNSUPPORTED_TARGET_OS.Advice: For a list of supported platforms, see the 'Supported platforms and architectures' section of the {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} User Guide.

UNSUPPORTED_TARGET_ARCH.Message: The target platform is not supported.
UNSUPPORTED_TARGET_ARCH.Explanation: The target machine implements an unsupported architecture ({arch}).
UNSUPPORTED_TARGET_ARCH.Advice: For a list of supported platforms, see the 'Supported platforms and architectures' section of the {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} User Guide.

UNSUPPORTED_TARGET_PLATFORM.Explanation: The target machine is an unsupported combination of OS and architecture ({os} {arch}).
UNSUPPORTED_TARGET_PLATFORM.Advice: For a list of supported platforms, see the 'Supported platforms and architectures' section of the {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} User Guide.

HOST_PLATFORM_FUNCTIONALITY_MISSING.Message: Required host-side functionality is unavailable on this platform.
HOST_PLATFORM_FUNCTIONALITY_MISSING.Explanation: The OS and architecture combination ({os} {arch}) does not provide the host-side functionality required for this operation.
HOST_PLATFORM_FUNCTIONALITY_MISSING.Advice: If the issue continues, contact Arm support.

USER_CANCELLATION_ERROR.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} stopped the operation after receiving a cancellation request.
USER_CANCELLATION_ERROR.Advice: If this occurred unexpectedly, contact Arm support.

USER_STOPPED_ERROR.Advice: If this occurred unexpectedly, contact Arm support.

CREATE_DEST_FILE.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot copy `{srcFilePath}` to `{dstFilePath}` because it cannot create the destination file. This can happen if the parent directory does not exist, you do not have write permissions, or the file system is corrupt.
CREATE_DEST_FILE.Advice: Check that the parent directory `{parentDir}` exists and you have write permissions for it. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot create the file, contact Arm support.

OPEN_SRC_FILE.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot open and copy the file.
OPEN_SRC_FILE.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot copy `{srcFilePath}` to `{dstFilePath}` because it cannot open the source file. This file might not exist, or you might not have permission to read it.
OPEN_SRC_FILE.Advice: Check that the `{srcFilePath}` file exists, and that you have read permissions. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot open and copy the file, contact Arm support.

COPY_CONTENTS.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} successfully opened `{srcFilePath}` and created `{dstFilePath}`. However, it cannot copy the contents of the first file to the second. The source file might be corrupt or an unexpected input/output error might have occurred. If the destination is on another machine, the connection might have closed.
COPY_CONTENTS.Advice: Check that the source file is not corrupted and that there is space on the destination drive. If the destination is on another machine, ensure that the connection is still open. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot copy the file contents, contact Arm support.

RUN_MACHINE_INFO_CMD.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot query the target machine architecture and operating system.
RUN_MACHINE_INFO_CMD.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} used the `uname -a` command to query the target machine architecture and OS, but the command failed.
RUN_MACHINE_INFO_CMD.Advice: Check that you can run `uname -a` on the target. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot query the target machine architecture and operating system, contact Arm support.

IDENTIFY_INFO_FROM_OUTPUT.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot identify the target machine architecture and operating system.
IDENTIFY_INFO_FROM_OUTPUT.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} used the `uname -a` command to identify the target machine architecture and OS, but it cannot extract this information from the output `{stdOut}`.
IDENTIFY_INFO_FROM_OUTPUT.Advice: Check that the output of the command contains a supported OS ('Linux') and architecture ('AArch64', 'arm64', or 'X86_64'). If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot identify the target machine architecture and operating system, contact Arm support.

NO_SHELL_FOUND.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot identify a shell to run the workload through.
NO_SHELL_FOUND.Explanation: The `--use-shell` flag requires a shell on the target to run the workload through. {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} tried to use the shell specified by the `{envVar}` environment variable, but this is not set or is empty. The fallback shell `{fallback}` also does not exist or failed to execute.
NO_SHELL_FOUND.Advice: Check that the `{envVar}` environment variable is set when connecting to the target manually using SSH. Alternatively, verify that the fallback shell `{fallback}` is usable. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot run the workload through a shell, contact Arm support.

MISSING_KEY_FOR_TARGET.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot find an authorized SSH private key for the target system.
MISSING_KEY_FOR_TARGET.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot identify an authorised private key for `{target}`. {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} checks {keyDirs} and attempted to use the following keys: {keyPaths}. The following SSH key formats are supported: OpenSSH, PEM-encoded PKCS#1, PEM-encoded PKCS#8, and PEM-encoded SEC1 EC.
MISSING_KEY_FOR_TARGET.Advice: Verify that an authorized SSH private key for `{target}` is available in the listed directories. If necessary, manually specify the private SSH key location. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot find a valid key, contact Arm support.

MISSING_KEY_FOR_JUMP.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot find an authorized SSH private key for `{jumpNode}`.
MISSING_KEY_FOR_JUMP.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot identify an authorized private key for the jump node at `{jumpNode}`. {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} checks {keyDirs} and attempted to use the following keys: {keyPaths}. The following SSH key formats are supported: OpenSSH, PEM-encoded PKCS#1, PEM-encoded PKCS#8, and PEM-encoded SEC1 EC.
MISSING_KEY_FOR_JUMP.Advice: Verify that an authorized SSH private key for `{jumpNode}` is available in the listed directories. If necessary, manually specify the private SSH key location. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot find a valid key, contact Arm support.

NO_VALID_KEYS.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot find any valid SSH private keys.
NO_VALID_KEYS.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot identify any valid private keys. {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} checks {keyDirs} and attempts to use keys from {keyPaths}. The following SSH key formats are supported: OpenSSH, PEM-encoded PKCS#1, PEM-encoded PKCS#8, and PEM-encoded SEC1 EC.
NO_VALID_KEYS.Advice: Verify that a valid SSH private key is available in the listed directories. If necessary, manually specify the private SSH key location. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot find a valid key, contact Arm support.

TCP_CONNECT_FAILED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} attempted to open a TCP connection to `{jumpNode}` on port `{port}` before searching for SSH keys, but the connection failed. The jump node might be offline, the port might be blocked, or the SSH service might not be listening.
TCP_CONNECT_FAILED.Advice: Check that the jump node is powered on and that SSH is listening on port `{port}`. Confirm you can connect manually, then retry the command. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot reach the jump node, contact Arm support.

TCP_CONNECT_FAILED_FOR_TARGET.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} attempted to open a TCP connection to `{target}` on port `{port}` before searching for SSH keys, but the connection failed. The target might be offline, the port might be blocked, or the SSH service might not be listening.
TCP_CONNECT_FAILED_FOR_TARGET.Advice: Check that the target is powered on and that SSH is listening on port `{port}`. Confirm you can connect manually, then retry the command. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot reach the target, contact Arm support.

LOCATE_KNOWN_HOSTS_FILE.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot locate the SSH known hosts file.
LOCATE_KNOWN_HOSTS_FILE.Explanation: Because your host key policy is not set to `ignore`, {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} must check the SSH known hosts file before starting an SSH connection to the target. {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot locate this file after searching in {locations}.
LOCATE_KNOWN_HOSTS_FILE.Advice: Check that an SSH known hosts file exists in one of the expected locations. Use the 'target update --help' command for more information on the different host key policies available. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot locate the file, contact Arm support.

OPEN_KNOWN_HOSTS.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot open the SSH known hosts file.
OPEN_KNOWN_HOSTS.Explanation: Because your host key policy is not set to `ignore`, {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} must check the SSH known hosts file before starting an SSH connection to the target. {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} located this file at `{filePath}`, but cannot open it.
OPEN_KNOWN_HOSTS.Advice: Check that the known hosts file exists at the specified location, and that you have permission to read it. Use the 'target update --help' command for more information on the different host key policies available. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot open the file, contact Arm support.

SANITIZE_KNOWN_HOSTS.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot sanitize the SSH known hosts file.
SANITIZE_KNOWN_HOSTS.Explanation: Because your host key policy is not set to `ignore`, {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} must check the SSH known hosts file before starting an SSH connection to the target. {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} located this file at `{filePath}`, but cannot create a temporary sanitized version.
SANITIZE_KNOWN_HOSTS.Advice: Check that you have write permissions in the parent directory of the known hosts file. Check the file for any formatting errors. Use the 'target update --help' command for more information on the different host key policies available. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot sanitize the file, contact Arm support.

KEY_FILE_NOT_READABLE.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot read the SSH private key file.
KEY_FILE_NOT_READABLE.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot read the SSH key file at `{path}` for the `{jumpNode}` node. The file might not exist, or it might not be readable due to permission issues.
KEY_FILE_NOT_READABLE.Advice: Verify that the SSH private key file exists and that you have permission to read it. If necessary, manually specify the private SSH key location for each jump node. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot read the private key file, contact Arm support.

KEY_FILE_NOT_READABLE_FOR_TARGET.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot read the SSH private key file.
KEY_FILE_NOT_READABLE_FOR_TARGET.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot read the SSH key file at `{path}` for `{target}`. The file might not exist, or it might not be readable due to permission issues.
KEY_FILE_NOT_READABLE_FOR_TARGET.Advice: Verify that the SSH private key file exists and that you have permission to read it. If necessary, manually specify the private SSH key location for the target. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot read the private key file, contact Arm support.

KEY_FILE_NOT_PARSABLE.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot parse the SSH private key file.
KEY_FILE_NOT_PARSABLE.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot parse the SSH key file at `{path}` for the `{jumpNode}` node. The following SSH key formats are supported: OpenSSH, PEM-encoded PKCS#1, PEM-encoded PKCS#8, and PEM-encoded SEC1 EC.
KEY_FILE_NOT_PARSABLE.Advice: Verify that the SSH private key file is formatted correctly using a supported format. If necessary, manually specify the private SSH key location for each jump node. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot parse the file, contact Arm support.

KEY_FILE_NOT_PARSABLE_FOR_TARGET.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot parse the SSH private key file.
KEY_FILE_NOT_PARSABLE_FOR_TARGET.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot parse the SSH key file at `{path}` for `{target}`. The following SSH key formats are supported: OpenSSH, PEM-encoded PKCS#1, PEM-encoded PKCS#8, and PEM-encoded SEC1 EC.
KEY_FILE_NOT_PARSABLE_FOR_TARGET.Advice: Verify that the SSH private key file is formatted correctly using a supported format. If necessary, manually specify the private SSH key location for the target. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot parse the file, contact Arm support.

KEY_FILE_INCORRECT_PASSPHRASE_FOR_TARGET.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot decrypt the SSH private key file.
KEY_FILE_INCORRECT_PASSPHRASE_FOR_TARGET.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot use the SSH key file at `{path}` for `{target}` because the passphrase supplied for this key is incorrect.
KEY_FILE_INCORRECT_PASSPHRASE_FOR_TARGET.Advice: Try again and enter the correct passphrase for the SSH private key. Configure a different key if you do not know the passphrase.

KEY_FILE_INCORRECT_PASSPHRASE.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot decrypt the SSH private key file.
KEY_FILE_INCORRECT_PASSPHRASE.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot use the SSH key file at `{path}` for the `{jumpNode}` node because the passphrase supplied for this key is incorrect.
KEY_FILE_INCORRECT_PASSPHRASE.Advice: Try again and enter the correct passphrase for the SSH private key. Configure a different key if you do not know the passphrase.

PASSWORD_INCORRECT.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot authenticate with `{host}` because the password was entered incorrectly
PASSWORD_INCORRECT.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} attempted to authenticate with `{host}` {maxAttempts} times using the password provided, but each attempt failed.
PASSWORD_INCORRECT.Advice: Try again and enter the correct password. Confirm that password authentication is enabled for the host. If you do not remember the password, reset it or use different credentials.

STRICT_KEY_UNKNOWN.Message: The host `{hostName}` does not exist in your known hosts file.
STRICT_KEY_UNKNOWN.Explanation: The host `{hostName}` is not listed in your known hosts file at `{knownHostsPath}`. {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} will not trust new hosts because the host key policy being used is `strict`.
STRICT_KEY_UNKNOWN.Advice: Add this host to your known hosts file, then try again. Use the `target update --help` command for more information on the different host key policies available.

STRICT_KEY_MISMATCH.Message: The public key provided by the host `{hostName}` does not match any known key in your known hosts file.
STRICT_KEY_MISMATCH.Explanation: The public key provided by the host `{hostName}` does not match any of the known keys for this host in your known hosts file at `{knownHostsPath}`. This host's key might have been updated, or this might indicate a security risk such as a man-in-the-middle attack.
STRICT_KEY_MISMATCH.Advice: Check with your system administrator. If you are sure that there are no concerns and that the key has been updated, remove the old key from your known hosts file, add the new one, then try again. Use the `target update --help` command for more information on the different host key policies available.

ACCEPT_NEW_KEY_MISMATCH.Message: The public key provided by the host `{hostName}` does not match any known key in your known hosts file.
ACCEPT_NEW_KEY_MISMATCH.Explanation: The public key provided by the host `{hostName}` does not match any of the known keys for this host in your known hosts file at `{knownHostsPath}`. This host's key might have been updated, or this might indicate a security risk such as a man-in-the-middle attack.
ACCEPT_NEW_KEY_MISMATCH.Advice: Check with your system administrator. If you are sure that there are no concerns and that the key has been updated, remove the old key from your known hosts file, then try again. Use the `target update --help` command for more information on the different host key policies available.

PROMPT_KEY_REJECTED.Message: The host key for `{hostName}` was rejected by the user.
PROMPT_KEY_REJECTED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} prompted to trust a new host key for `{hostName}`, but the user rejected it.
PROMPT_KEY_REJECTED.Advice: If you trust this host, retry and accept the key or add it to your known hosts file.

KEY_REVOKED.Message: The public key provided by the host `{hostName}` is marked as revoked in your known hosts file.
KEY_REVOKED.Explanation: The public key provided by the host `{hostName}` is marked as revoked in your known hosts file at `{knownHostsPath}`. This means that the key has been explicitly marked as not usable. This might be because the key is compromised, stolen or deprecated.
KEY_REVOKED.Advice: If `{hostName}` is a jump host, try removing or replacing this host from the chain of jumps. Otherwise, use a different target, or contact your system administrator.

DIRECT_CONN_FAILED_NET.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect to `{hostName}` using SSH because a network route to this host cannot be found.
DIRECT_CONN_FAILED_NET.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect directly to the host `{hostName}` because your local machine cannot determine a network route to reach it. This might be because you are not connected to the internet or the required VPN, or your routing tables are misconfigured.
DIRECT_CONN_FAILED_NET.Advice: Check that you are connected to the internet by running `ping 8.8.8.8`. If `{hostName}` requires access through a VPN, make sure that you are connected to it, then try again. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot determine a network route to this host, contact Arm support.

DIRECT_CONN_FAILED_DNS.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect to `{hostName}` using SSH because the DNS lookup failed.
DIRECT_CONN_FAILED_DNS.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect directly to the host `{hostName}` because this hostname cannot be resolved. It might not exist, or the DNS server might not be reachable, which might indicate that you are not connected to the internet or the required VPN.
DIRECT_CONN_FAILED_DNS.Advice: Check that you are connected to the internet by running `ping 8.8.8.8`. Ensure that the hostname `{hostName}` is correct and resolvable from your local machine. If this host requires access through a VPN, make sure that you are connected to it, then try again. If the DNS lookup still fails, contact Arm support.

DIRECT_CONN_FAILED_TIMEOUT.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect to `{address}` using SSH because the address did not respond.
DIRECT_CONN_FAILED_TIMEOUT.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect directly to `{address}` because this address did not respond within the timeout window. Possible causes include this host being offline or its SSH server not listening on port {portNum}, or your local machine not being connected to the required VPN.
DIRECT_CONN_FAILED_TIMEOUT.Advice: Check that you can manually connect to the host `{hostName}` using SSH. Check that this host's SSH server is listening on port {portNum}. If this host requires access through a VPN, make sure that you are connected to it, then try again. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot connect to `{address}`, contact Arm support.

DIRECT_CONN_FAILED_ALGS.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect to `{hostName}` using SSH because no compatible cryptographic algorithms could be negotiated.
DIRECT_CONN_FAILED_ALGS.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect directly to the host `{hostName}` because this host was not able to agree with your local machine on a common set of cryptographic algorithms to use. One of the machines might only support outdated algorithms, or might be configured to use a restricted algorithm set for security reasons. `{hostName}` offered: {hostAlgs}. Your local machine offered: {localAlgs}.
DIRECT_CONN_FAILED_ALGS.Advice: Check with your system administrator. You might need to update the configuration of the SSH server on the host `{hostName}` to include at least one key exchange, cipher, or MAC algorithm supported by your host machine. If algorithm negotiation still fails, contact Arm support.

DIRECT_CONN_FAILED_PASSWORD_AUTH.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect to `{hostName}` using SSH because the provided password was rejected.
DIRECT_CONN_FAILED_PASSWORD_AUTH.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect directly to the host `{hostName}` because the provided SSH username and password were rejected. The password might be incorrect or the account might be locked.
DIRECT_CONN_FAILED_PASSWORD_AUTH.Advice: Ensure that the username and password for `{hostName}` are correct and that the account is unlocked. If the password continues to be rejected, contact your system administrator.

DIRECT_CONN_FAILED_KEY_AUTH.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect to `{hostName}` using SSH because the provided SSH key was rejected.
DIRECT_CONN_FAILED_KEY_AUTH.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect directly to the host `{hostName}` because the provided SSH key was rejected. The key might not be authorized for this user account or the account might be locked.
DIRECT_CONN_FAILED_KEY_AUTH.Advice: Ensure that your SSH key is correct, that the key is authorized on the host `{hostName}`, and that the account is unlocked. If the key continues to be rejected, contact your system administrator.

DIRECT_CONN_PASSWORD_AUTH_DISABLED.Message: The host `{hostName}` does not allow password authentication.
DIRECT_CONN_PASSWORD_AUTH_DISABLED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} contacted the SSH server on `{hostName}` to determine permitted authentication methods. The server does not allow password authentication.
DIRECT_CONN_PASSWORD_AUTH_DISABLED.Advice: Configure the target to use an authentication method that `{hostName}` supports, or enable password authentication on the SSH server before trying again.

DIRECT_CONN_KEY_AUTH_DISABLED.Message: The host `{hostName}` does not allow public key authentication.
DIRECT_CONN_KEY_AUTH_DISABLED.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} contacted the SSH server on `{hostName}` to determine permitted authentication methods. The server does not allow public key authentication.
DIRECT_CONN_KEY_AUTH_DISABLED.Advice: Configure the target to use an authentication method that `{hostName}` supports, or enable public key authentication on the SSH server before trying again.

DIRECT_CONN_FAILED_UNKNOWN.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} encountered an error while connecting directly to the host `{hostName}`. Possible causes include this host sending an unexpected pre-authentication banner, the firewall blocking the connection, or another connection error occurring.
DIRECT_CONN_FAILED_UNKNOWN.Advice: Check that you can manually connect to the host `{hostName}` using SSH. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot connect to this host, contact Arm support.

JUMP_CONN_FAILED_NET.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect to `{nextHost}` from `{prevHost}` using SSH because a network route to `{nextHost}` cannot be found.
JUMP_CONN_FAILED_NET.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect to the host `{nextHost}` from the previous jump node `{prevHost}` because this jump node cannot determine a network route to reach `{nextHost}`. The previous jump node `{prevHost}` might not be connected to the required VPN to reach `{nextHost}`, or its routing tables might be misconfigured.
JUMP_CONN_FAILED_NET.Advice: If necessary, make sure that `{prevHost}` is connected to the required VPN to reach `{nextHost}`, then try again. If {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} still cannot determine a network route to `{nextHost}`, contact Arm support.

JUMP_CONN_FAILED_DNS.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect to `{nextHost}` from `{prevHost}` using SSH because the DNS lookup failed.
JUMP_CONN_FAILED_DNS.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect to the host `{nextHost}` from the previous jump node `{prevHost}` because the hostname `{nextHost}` cannot be resolved. This hostname might not exist, or the DNS server might not be reachable from the previous jump node `{prevHost}`, which might indicate that it is not connected to the required VPN.
JUMP_CONN_FAILED_DNS.Advice: Ensure that the hostname `{nextHost}` is correct and resolvable from the previous jump node `{prevHost}`. If `{nextHost}` requires access through a VPN, make sure that `{prevHost}` is connected to it, then try again. If the DNS lookup still fails, contact Arm support.

JUMP_CONN_FAILED_TIMEOUT.Message: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect to `{nextAddress}` from `{prevHost}` using SSH because `{nextAddress}` did not respond.
JUMP_CONN_FAILED_TIMEOUT.Explanation: {$PRODUCT_FULL_NAME} cannot connect to `{nextAddress}` from the previous jump node `{prevHost}` because `{nextAddress}` did not respond within the timeout window. Possible causes include this host being offline or its SSH server not listening on port {nextPort}, or the previous jump node `{prevHost}` not being connected to the required VPN to reach `{nextHost}`.
JUMP_CONN_FAILED_TIMEOUT.Advice: Check that you can manually connect to `{nextHost}` from the previous jump node `{prevHost}` using SSH.
